title: Watch page comments + remove Viewer Timer UI

requirements.summary: Remove Viewer Timer UI and all timer-related wiring from the Watch page on mobile and desktop layouts.
acceptanceCriteria: When viewing any media on the Watch page, there is no Viewer Timer card, no timer inputs/buttons, and no 'Viewer Timer' label anywhere in the rendered UI.
The Watch page still plays media normally and shows title/date/duration metadata without errors.
There is no timer-related logic executed from WatchPage (e.g., no onTimerEnd/pause callback wiring from a timer component).

file_operations.description: Remove the ViewerTimer import, timer callback logic (including any pause-on-timer-end wiring), and all timer JSX blocks for both mobile and desktop so no timer-related controls/text render anywhere.

requirements.summary: Add React Query hooks for fetching and posting comments keyed by media title, with cache invalidation and clear error handling.
acceptanceCriteria: A Watch-page comments query is keyed by media title (e.g., ['comments', title]) and refetches when the title changes.
Posting a comment triggers an update so the new comment appears without requiring a manual page refresh.
If the backend actor is unavailable, the comments UI shows a clear English error message instead of failing silently.

file_operations.description: Add comment-related React Query hooks that call the backend actor methods to fetch comments and create a comment, using a query key of ['comments', mediaTitle] and invalidating/refetching that key on successful post; ensure actor-unavailable cases throw a clear English error message.

requirements.summary: Add a Watch page Comments section to list comments and allow signed-in users to post, while guests can read only with a sign-in prompt.
acceptanceCriteria: The Watch page shows a 'Comments' section beneath the video player/metadata area.
If there are no comments, the UI displays an English empty state such as 'No comments yet. Be the first to comment.'
Signed-in users see a text input (textarea) and a 'Post comment' button; submitting posts the comment and clears the input on success.
Guests can see the comment list (and empty state), but cannot post; the UI shows an English message such as 'Sign in to post a comment.'
Posted comments render with their text and a readable timestamp; author display uses the commenter profile name when available, otherwise a safe fallback label in English.

file_operations.description: Create a CommentsSection component that uses the new comment React Query hooks to render: a 'Comments' heading, loading/error states (English), an empty state message, and a newest-first list with readable timestamps; use the authorization component’s frontend guidance (Internet Identity state + user profile) to detect guests vs signed-in users and to show an English sign-in prompt while disabling/hiding the submit action for guests. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Render the new CommentsSection beneath the video player/metadata area and pass the current media title as the comments key; ensure the section remains visible to guests for read-only access. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.
